title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer backoff ordering race causing regional failover thrashing
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: During a production incident (INT-5478) we observed the SLO enforcer enter a pathological loop when regional failover events and aggressive client backoff overlapped. Symptoms were repeated region-level circuit-breaker opens, rapid failovers, and load-shedding thrashing which caused elevated 5xx and request timeouts for impacted customers. Root cause: a race between the backoff queue ordering logic and the regional failover coordinator where concurrent backoff updates could reorder tasks and cause duplicate failover candidates to be scheduled. The enforcer's eviction path was not idempotent when entries moved between in-memory queues during failover, which allowed multiple workers to act on the same logical request and trigger repeated failovers. What this PR does: fixes deterministic ordering and idempotency in the SLO enforcer backoff path and hardens regional failover coordination to prevent thrash. Key changes are: - Add sequence numbers to backoff entries and make queue reordering deterministic (stable sort by sequence then timestamp). - Make eviction and failover scheduling idempotent by attaching a scheduling token (opaque UUID) and using compare-and-swap when transitioning state. - Introduce a lightweight leader guard in regional failover coordinator so only one worker performs the failover decisions for a region during a window. - Add hysteresis to the per-region circuit-breaker backoff to avoid immediate re-opening after a close (configurable via slo-enforcer.hysteresis_ms). - Improve metrics/tracing: added metrics slo_enforcer.scheduled_failovers_total, slo_enforcer.duplicate_evictions_total and tracing spans around queue transitions for investigation. - Add unit and integration tests that reproduce the original race (ordering_test.go and region_failover_integration_test.go). - Add a short rollout plan and a rollback knob (feature flag slo_enforcer.strict_ordering=false) for emergency revert. Testing and verification: local unit tests (ordering/eviction) added; integration test simulates concurrent backoff updates + regional coordinator and asserts single failover decision. CI: all checks passed after one re-run of flaky unit test (see ci_checks). We ran a canary rollout to 10% of capacity in us-west-2 for 2 hours and observed stable circuit-breaker metrics and no repeat failovers. After canary we performed a gradual rollout to remaining regions. Rollout plan and post-merge steps: - Merge to main and deploy slo-enforcer service with feature flag default enabled. - Monitor slo_enforcer.duplicate_evictions_total and region_failover.count for 48 hours. - If regressions, flip feature flag slo_enforcer.strict_ordering=false and rollback service version. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration test reproducing race - [x] Canary verification (10% us-west-2) - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Rollback knob Related: ENG-4821, SRE-312, incident INT-5478

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain why we chose sequence numbers vs CAS on timestamps? I worry about clock skew making timestamps unreliable.

Maya Chen: Sequence numbers are generated by the originating enqueuer and are monotonic for each request; we use stable sort (seq,timestamp) to retain deterministic behavior even when timestamps have minor jitter.
Sofia Martinez: +1 on idempotency, but please add a metric for duplicate evictions (added slo_enforcer.duplicate_evictions_total).
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good; integration test repro is valuable. Please ensure the leader guard times out quickly to avoid single-point delay.
Maya Chen: Updated leader guard to use optimistic lease with 5s default TTL and added test to validate timeout behavior.
ci_checks: unit tests: flaky at first -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Fixes a race in the SLO enforcer backoff/ordering path that could cause repeated regional failovers and load-shedding thrash. Adds deterministic ordering, idempotent eviction, leader guard for regional failover, and hysteresis to circuit-breakers. Includes metrics for duplicate evictions and a rollback feature flag.
